Book correction: As printed, this identity is true only when its right side is positive, for example \frac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \frac{3\pi}{2}. For acute \alpha it fails: at \alpha = 0 the left side is 1 but the right side is \frac{0 + 1}{0 - 1} = -1. In general the left side equals \left|\frac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} + \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} - \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}\right|; for -\frac{\pi}{2} < \alp
